lesson.butterfly_symmetry_study.title: Butterfly Symmetry & Proportion
lesson.butterfly_symmetry_study.summary: Use a center axis, compare wing sizes and layer a few vein lines to build a more controlled butterfly.
lesson.butterfly_symmetry_study.step.bod: Build a narrow body and add a light center axis to organize the butterfly.
lesson.butterfly_symmetry_study.help.bod: Keep the body centered and use the axis as a visual ruler for left and right.
lesson.butterfly_symmetry_study.step.upp: Draw the two upper wings and compare their height, width and outer tips.
lesson.butterfly_symmetry_study.help.upp: Check the left and right tips against the center axis before you close each contour.
lesson.butterfly_symmetry_study.step.low: Add the smaller lower wings and relate their size to the upper pair.
lesson.butterfly_symmetry_study.help.low: Let the lower wings sit below the widest part of the upper wings and stay visibly smaller.
lesson.butterfly_symmetry_study.complete: The full silhouette now has a clear size hierarchy.
lesson.butterfly_symmetry_study.step.vei: Layer a few paired vein lines from the body toward the wings.
lesson.butterfly_symmetry_study.help.vei: Use fewer clean lines instead of filling every space. Match the general direction on both sides.
lesson.butterfly_symmetry_study.complete: Your butterfly has controlled structure and layered detail.
